title: sync: preserve original errors from --keep-going
body:
With --keep-going the individual copy errors were only logged, and run() returned a generic sentinel, so the exit code could no longer tell anything apart: even a sync where every failure was a missing image exited 1 instead of the documented 2.

The errors are now collected. When they are all image-not-found errors they are returned joined, so isNotFoundImageError still matches and the exit code is 2. For a mixed set of failures the generic sentinel is kept, formatting the individual errors with %s instead of %w so the joined tree can't be misclassified as "not found".

Ephemeral COPR build failed. @containers/packit-build please check.

The distinction is documented globally, not per-command — skopeo(1) has an EXIT STATUS section:

> **1** Generic error, details can be found in the error message.
> **2** The input image cannot be found. Note that this is best effort and for remote registries the status often cannot be reliably reported.

Plain sync already behaves exactly that way today: without --keep-going the first failure is returned as-is, so a missing image exits 2 and anything else exits 1. The only path that broke that contract was --keep-going collapsing everything into 1 — that's what motivated this PR.

On your mixed case: that's exactly why it returns 1 there. "2" is best-effort per the doc, and it only claims something when every failure was a missing image; the moment one failure is something else, it's a generic error with details in the message — which is literally what the doc says 1 is.

So all this PR does is make --keep-going stop violating the documented contract for the all-not-found case. If you'd rather have --keep-going at a flat 1 regardless, I can flatten it and keep just the joined error detail — but then plain sync and --keep-going would disagree on the same input, which is the part I wanted to fix.
